subject: Async job completion envelope — SLA exception & idempotency mitigation
messages:
From: Joel Pratt <joel.pratt@datawave.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Hart <sylvia.hart@datawave.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Async job completion — long-tail run times and retry duplication

Hi Stephanie,

We're seeing a growing number of async/batch inference jobs for our nightly pipeline take well beyond the 24-hour window we expected — several runs are in the 36–48 hour range. That has two knock-on effects for us: 1) our consumers time out and re-submit, which results in duplicate processing, and 2) the uncertainty makes our SLAs to our customers difficult to keep.

Can Redwood grant an exception to the job-completion SLO for these long-tail runs while we work through root cause? If not a formal exception, we need clear guidance on retry/backoff and an idempotency pattern that will prevent duplicates across retries.

I've attached a small sample of job IDs and timestamps so you can see the distribution (datawave_job_samples.csv).

Appreciate any immediate mitigations we can apply while engineering digs in.

Thanks,
Joel Pratt
Head of Platform Engineering
DataWave Analytics

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Joel Pratt <joel.pratt@datawave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T13:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Async job completion — long-tail run times and retry duplication

Joel — thanks for the clear data and the sample. We take long-tail jobs seriously and sorry for the operational pain this is causing your team.

Immediate actions we can take this week:
- Temporary SLA exception: we can provision a 30-day completion-envelope exception for jobs classified as "long-tail" (>=24h projected) tied to the attached form. This gives us runway to remediate without reprovisioning credits.
- Short-term mitigation: increase server-side retry window + exponential backoff on our end and provide you a recommended client-side backoff window to avoid re-submission storms.
- Idempotency: we will push a spec for async idempotency tokens (recommended: client-provided job_id + server-side dedupe window) and an interim server-side dedupe flag to reduce duplicates.

Ben, can you confirm commercial/credit side? Karthik/Marissa — can you validate feasibility of a temporary dedicated slot for their nightly jobs and draft the idempotency spec? Joel — please confirm whether the attached CSV is representative and whether you can sign the SLA exception form if we draft one.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Joel Pratt <joel.pratt@datawave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Async job completion — long-tail run times and retry duplication

Joel — digging into this with the infra team. High-level proposal: 

1) Idempotency model (attached: idempotency_spec_v1.md)
   - Client supplies job_id (UUID) with each async submission.
   - Server keeps a sliding dedupe window (configurable, default 7 days for batch jobs) keyed by job_id + model_version + input_hash.
   - If duplicate arrives within window, server returns 'duplicate-accepted' with original job handle.

2) Retry/backoff guidance
   - Client: linear backoff 30m -> 1h -> 2h -> 4h, stop after 6 attempts unless client explicitly reconciles.
   - Server: honor client retries but do not auto-retry externally unless the server-side transient error rate exceeds threshold.

3) Short-term capacity mitigation
   - Provision a temporary dedicated pool for their nightly job class (capacity increase) to reduce queueing.

4) Observability hooks
   - We will enable job-level traces and a per-job latency histogram you can query via the Console.

Timeline: we can ship server-side dedupe and the observability hooks in ~7 business days; provisioned pool can be available in 48–72 hours. If you agree, we'll start the pool request and give you an ETA for the dedupe push.

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Joel Pratt <joel.pratt@datawave.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Async job completion — long-tail run times and retry duplication

Joel — quick operational note. We created a draft SLA exception amendment and uploaded it for signature (DocuSign link below). The amendment documents: exception window (up to 72 hours for qualifying long-tail jobs), expected remediation milestones, and a one-time 10% service credit applied if we miss the amended envelope during the exception period.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.example/docusign/XYZ-998877

We'll also kick off provisioning for a temporary dedicated pool to run during your 02:00–06:00 UTC nightly batch window. If you sign the amendment, provisioning begins immediately and Karthik's team will prioritize the dedupe rollout.

Attachments: SLA_exception_form.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Joel Pratt <joel.pratt@datawave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Async job completion — long-tail run times and retry duplication

Marissa / Karthik — thanks, that path looks good. A couple of follow-ups:

- While waiting for the dedupe rollout, what's the recommended client-side behavior so we don't accidentally spawn multiple downstream workflows? If we implement the client side backoff you proposed, will dedupe on your side still protect us if a retry crosses an in-flight processing window?
- Attached is an expanded sample list (I included job metadata) — we've anonymized customer IDs but retained timestamps.

If DocuSign is the fastest way to get the pool live, I'll push it internally and sign today.

Best,
Joel

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Joel Pratt <joel.pratt@datawave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Async job completion — long-tail run times and retry duplication

Joel — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming:

- DocuSign amendment signed this morning (I see the completed envelope). We applied a 30-day exception window starting 2027-05-28; the dedicated pool will be live in the next 36 hours.
- We will implement the server-side dedupe as scoped in idempotency_spec_v1.md (target: production toggle in 7 business days).
- Commercial: Ben has approved a one-time 10% service credit if we miss the amended envelope during the exception window — you'll see that on the next invoice.
- Client guidance: adopt the backoff pattern in Karthik's note and include a stable job_id for each submission; this plus server dedupe will prevent duplicate downstream processing in >95% of observed cases.

Closing action items:
- Marissa: confirm pool activation ETA and share Console link to the job-level traces.
- Karthik: schedule a short runbook sync with Joel's infra team for Tuesday 2027-06-01.
- Ben: confirm credit applied once the exception period completes.

I'll leave this thread open until the dedupe gate is in prod, but marking the immediate escalation as acknowledged and actioned. Thanks everyone.

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
